  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE,
  render = function(x, ...) {

    knitr::knit_print(x, ...)
  }
)
# The code runs only when SeuratData and both datasets are installed, so the
# rest of the website still builds if they are unavailable.
has.seuratdata <- requireNamespace("SeuratObject", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("SeuratData", quietly = TRUE) &&
  all(c("stxBrain.SeuratData", "ifnb.SeuratData") %in%
        rownames(utils::installed.packages()))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = has.seuratdata)
```

cat("> **Note:** this copy of the page was built without SeuratData, so the code",
    "below shows no output.\n")
```

Most single-cell data in R lives in Seurat objects. This page shows how
`extract_NICHESInputs_Seurat()` turns two real Seurat objects into NICHESv2
inputs. They are the same two datasets the tutorials use, and these are the steps
that made the tutorial inputs.

The objects come from [SeuratData](https://github.com/satijalab/seurat-data),
which the Satija Lab maintains. The tutorials don't need it, because they
download the finished inputs with `download_NICHESv2_data()`.

## Install SeuratData

SeuratData isn't on CRAN. Run this once; the downloads are about 143 MB for
`stxBrain` and 413 MB for `ifnb`. SeuratData also installs the Seurat package, so
the first install can take a while.

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
install.packages(c("remotes", "SeuratObject"))
remotes::install_github("satijalab/seurat-data")
SeuratData::InstallData(c("stxBrain", "ifnb"))
```

```{r load}
library(NICHESv2)
library(SeuratObject)
library(SeuratData)
```

SeuratData objects keep the Seurat version they were saved with.
`extract_NICHESInputs_Seurat()` reads both V4 and V5 objects, so you don't need
to update them first. The spatial object below is V5 and the non-spatial one is
V4.

## A spatial object: Visium mouse brain

`stxBrain` holds four sections, and the spatial tutorial uses `anterior1`.

```{r spatial}
data("anterior1")

spatial <- extract_NICHESInputs_Seurat(
  seurat.obj = anterior1,
  assay      = "Spatial",
  layer      = "counts",
  verbose    = FALSE
)
dim(spatial$count.mtx)
```

Spatial coordinates sit in the image part of the Seurat object, so add them to
the metadata as `x` and `y`. Matching by barcode keeps every spot aligned.

```{r coords}
coords <- GetTissueCoordinates(anterior1)
spatial$meta.data$x <- coords[rownames(spatial$meta.data), "x"]
spatial$meta.data$y <- coords[rownames(spatial$meta.data), "y"]
head(spatial$meta.data[, c("x", "y")], 3)
```

## A non-spatial object: stimulated PBMCs

```{r nonspatial}
data("ifnb")

nonspatial <- extract_NICHESInputs_Seurat(
  seurat.obj = ifnb,
  assay      = "RNA",
  layer      = "counts",
  verbose    = FALSE
)
dim(nonspatial$count.mtx)
table(nonspatial$meta.data$stim)
```

No coordinates are needed here, because non-spatial mode pairs cells by sampling
within cell types.

## Next steps

`spatial` and `nonspatial` hold the same inputs that `download_NICHESv2_data()`
returns. Pass either to `create_NICHESObject()` and continue with the
[spatial tutorial](spatial-tutorial.html) or the
[non-spatial tutorial](nonspatial-tutorial.html). For other Seurat options, such
as choosing a layer, see [Input formats](input-formats.html).
